scope: Embedding provider selection and tenant batch boundary; not complete platform security assurance.

findings.initial_state: Explicit embedding providers bypassed session registry ownership, and both indexing and semantic query embedding bypassed the application privacy ceiling.
findings.change: Require an owned registered provider, a configured ceiling and one unambiguous model within the provider and model privacy limits; recheck ownership, ceiling and embedding space after the asynchronous call.
findings.evidence: mission19-evidence/embedding-before.txt records five fail-first cases. Focused tests verify no outbound invocation on rejection and reject changed configuration before persistence or scoring.
findings.limitations: The first configured registry ceiling is fixed against public setter and bootstrap elevation; arbitrary in-process private-state tampering, tenant-specific ceilings, endpoint egress, tenant authorization of each indexing invocation, atomic configuration and in-flight cancellation remain unproven.

findings.initial_state: A single embedding request could combine chunks belonging to different organizations.
findings.change: Reject missing or mixed organization identities before invoking the provider; PostgreSQL integration indexes separate tenant batches.
findings.evidence: mission19-evidence/embedding-mixed-tenant-before.txt; focused regression and PostgreSQL pgvector integration.
findings.limitations: Same-tenant batching does not itself authorize the caller or prove tenant-specific provider/credential isolation.

findings.initial_state: Runtime mutation, registry clearing and rebootstrap could raise the original application privacy limit; chat routing also trusted a model privacy declaration when its provider was less private.
findings.change: Preserve the first configured ceiling for the registry lifetime, reject escalations before clearing providers, fail closed after a cleared ceiling and enforce both provider and model privacy during chat selection.
findings.evidence: Fail-first tests in mission19-evidence/deployment-ceiling-before.txt and chat-provider-privacy-before.txt; focused and broader security regression tests.
findings.limitations: Not a sandbox against arbitrary Python private-state mutation; per-tenant policy, complete recovery/atomic bootstrap and layered network restrictions remain open.

findings.initial_state: Async DNS lookup yielded to other tasks, allowing a restrictive snapshot to be replaced with a permissive snapshot before destination validation.
findings.change: Validate the same DNS answers against both the entry snapshot and current snapshot; fail closed if either rejects.
findings.evidence: mission19-evidence/egress-dns-race-before.txt, egress-broad.txt and egress-webhook-integration.txt demonstrate the deterministic race, regression and webhook no-client-created behavior.
findings.limitations: Process-wide snapshots still conflate application/database ownership, explicit caller overrides are not ownership enforcement, and policy changes after pinning or during network activity are not prevented. This is not complete isolation or cancellation.

open: tenant-specific and immutable deployment-wide policies beyond application registry
complete concurrency and lifecycle security assurance
